newsitem.title: UK: Cargo wholesaler ICM sees 30pct rise in 97 revenue.
newsitem.headline: Cargo wholesaler ICM sees 30pct rise in 97 revenue.

text.p: UK airfreight wholesaler International Cargo Marketing (ICM) forecasts it will achieve a 30 percent increase in turnover this year on the eight million stg recorded for 1996.

Managing director of the British Midland Airways division, Terry Greetham, told Reuters that most ICM destinations had shown both volume and revenue increases so far this year, apart from North America and to a lesser extent Asia and Australia.
"We have noticed some weakening of our business to North America over recent months. It could be because of the strong pound against the dollar but I cannot say for sure," he said.
"As for Asia and Australasia, there has also been a slight weakening but this is of no great cause for concern. In fact, Hong Kong and Korea are growing markets for ICM," he noted.
Greetham added that Johannesburg is ICM's major destination in terms of volumes and revenue earnings and that Continental Europe was becoming an increasingly important market.
ICM was formed in 1988 and now has associations with more than 200 airlines and publishes a monthly wholesale tariff featuring 800 destinations worldwide.
"Because we have always gone for providing the broadest range of destinations we possibly could, future expansion must be aimed at increasing our market share," he said.

Greetham said that ICM's main ex-UK global wholesale competitor was Air Menzies International (AMI) and that other rivals in specific market sectors were Achilles Freight, PBL Aircargo (especially regarding UK-North America traffic) and Dunwoody Airline Services. -Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
